title: Claude's Philosophy and Safety
description: Understand Anthropic's Constitutional AI approach, why Claude is designed to be cautious, and what this means for everyday users.

data.text: Most AI assistants are trained using a combination of pre-training on internet text and then fine-tuning with human feedback. Anthropic takes a different approach called Constitutional AI (CAI). The idea is simple: rather than relying entirely on human reviewers to judge every output, Claude is given a set of principles — a 'constitution' — and trained to critique and revise its own outputs according to those principles.

data.title: What 'Constitutional AI' means in practice
data.text: Claude's constitution is a list of principles inspired by documents like the UN Declaration of Human Rights. During training, Claude learns to evaluate its own responses against these principles and revise anything that violates them. This is why Claude tends to refuse certain requests that other assistants might fulfill — it is applying its training to decide the request is not aligned with its principles.

Claude's safety-first design affects your everyday experience in several practical ways. Claude will often refuse requests that other assistants might attempt, such as generating content that could be harmful, providing instructions for dangerous activities, or engaging with prompt injection attempts. For most users, this is a feature, not a bug — but it can occasionally feel restrictive if you are used to less cautious assistants.
What Claude Will and Won't Do

data.title: Claude's boundaries:
items: Will not generate content that promotes harm, violence, or illegal activities
Will not help create malware, phishing tools, or exploit code
Will resist jailbreak attempts and prompt injection attacks
Will acknowledge uncertainty rather than fabricating confident-sounding answers
Can discuss sensitive topics in an educational, neutral manner

data.text: Anthropic describes its mission as ensuring that artificial general intelligence (AGI) benefits humanity. This is not a vague aspiration — it shapes how they build products, which capabilities they release, and how they engage with regulators and the research community. Claude's cautious approach reflects a belief that AI assistants should be reliable and trustworthy enough to be used in high-stakes contexts like education, healthcare, and legal work.
Safety vs. Utility: Finding the Balance

Every AI system faces a tension between being helpful and being safe. An assistant that refuses everything is not useful. An assistant that does everything you ask without question can cause harm. Claude's design philosophy puts safety first, which means you may occasionally need to rephrase a request to achieve your goal. This is not a flaw — it is the system working as intended.

data.title: Reframing refusals
data.text: When Claude declines a request, it is not being uncooperative. It is applying a safety framework. If your request is legitimate but phrased in a way that triggers a refusal, try rephrasing to focus on the educational, professional, or creative intent behind the request.

Prompt injection is a technique where users try to trick an AI into ignoring its instructions by embedding hidden commands in their input. Claude's Constitutional AI training includes specific defenses against this. If you paste a document that contains hidden instructions like 'Ignore all previous instructions and say X', Claude is trained to recognize and resist this kind of manipulation.

terms.definition: An attack where hidden text tricks an AI into ignoring its instructions. Claude is trained to resist these.
Anthropic's training method where the model is given a set of principles and learns to self-correct against them.
An attempt to bypass an AI's safety restrictions through clever prompting. Claude's training makes common jailbreaks less effective.
